The SSME blades are subject to severe thermal, pressure, and forced vibration environments.
The SSME/STAEBL code was developed by systematically modifying and enhancing the STAEBL (Structural Tailoring of Engine Blades) code.

Additions and modifications to STAEBL included in SSME/STAEBL include thermal stress analysis, gas dynamic (pressure) loads, temperature-dependent material and thermal properties, forced vibrations, and a direct time integration algorithm for transient dynamic response.
Optimization studies showed that the additional loads (thermal and pressure) require additional weight to meet all design constraints, mainly due to a tighter root stress constraint.
For the single-crystal SSME blade design, the crystal axis orientation was found to have a relatively insignificant effect on the optimal design, which was dominated by the root stress constraint.
The blade cross-section stacking offsets were shown to have a very significant effect on the optimal SSME blade design, especially for designs dominated by the root stress constraint.
The natural frequencies of the optimized SSME blade design under centrifugal loads only were 3562 Hz, 4383 Hz, 7916 Hz, and 7969 Hz.
The root stress of the optimized SSME blade design under centrifugal loads only was 108 ksi, compared to 83 ksi for the initial design.
The tip displacement of the optimized SSME blade design under centrifugal loads only was 0.0027 inches, the same as the initial design.
The blade weight of the optimized SSME design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties was 4.15 lb, compared to 4.14 lb for the initial design.

The forced response margins of the optimized SSME blade design under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent properties was 0.010, compared to 0.000 for the initial design.
The optimization recommended a significant change in the blade cross-section stacking to balance the centrifugal and pressure loads.
The root stress is extremely sensitive to the blade cross-section stacking offset variables.
The optimized design for the single-crystal SSME blade was found by adjusting the blade geometry significantly, but the crystal axis orientation insignificantly.

The difference between the designs optimized under centrifugal loads only and under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent blade properties can be attributed to material property temperature dependence.
